text:
The Canucks are now winless in eight (0-7-1), and Tuesday at Rogers Arena looked like a team that has stopped expecting different. Vancouver pulled even three times, at 1-1, 2-2 and 3-3, but never once led, and Carolina took the game with three goals in the third period for a 6-3 win.

The score understates the gap. Carolina took 78 shot attempts to Vancouver's 38 and put 44 shots on goal to the Canucks' 17. Expected goals, a measure of how good each team's chances were, came out 4.96 to 1.67 for the Hurricanes. By the share of simulated replays of every shot that each side wins, Carolina deserved the win 85 percent of the time. The first two periods were close, with Carolina ahead only 1.89 to 1.23 in expected goals. The third was not: 3.07 to 0.44.

Nikolaj Ehlers had two goals and an assist, and Logan Stankoven did the same, scoring the first goal and the last. Nicolas Deslauriers scored twice, including the 4-3 goal early in the third. Jackson Blake added three assists and had a 27 percent chance stopped by Leevi Meriläinen, who faced 43 shots. Vancouver's best moment may have been Max Sasson's 3-3 goal on a 3 percent chance. Carolina was 0 for 5 on the power play, and Vancouver scored on its only man advantage that mattered, Jonathan Lekkerimäki's goal with two seconds left in the first period.

Vancouver stays winless through eight games and now has an earlier 7-2 loss to Carolina on Oct. 8 on its ledger too. The Hurricanes, who won both meetings, leave with their second lopsided result of the season against the Canucks.
